paper.title_en: Phase-Resolved X-ray Polarimetry of LMC X-1: Enhanced Polarization at Inferior Conjunction
paper.abstract_en: We present a phase-resolved X-ray polarimetric analysis of the extragalactic black hole X-ray binary LMC X-1, a classical high/soft state source with a well-characterized accretion disk and an ionization cone/inferred jet. Previous X-ray polarimetry gave only orbit-averaged upper limits on the polarization fraction, leaving any orbital-phase dependence unexplored. We aim to probe how this polarization depends on orbital phase and to identify the origin of the polarized emission. We analyzed simultaneous IXPE, NICER, and NuSTAR observations taken in October 2022. We measured the polarization degree and angle in different energy bands as a function of orbital phase, performed spectro-polarimetric modeling to identify the emitting components, and modeled the phase modulation of the Stokes parameters with a cosine function. The polarization depends on orbital phase: during inferior conjunction (phase from -0.1 to 0.1), the polarization degree is (4.2+/-1.1)% in 2-3 keV and (3.4+/-0.8)% in 2-8 keV, with polarization angles of (46+/-8) and (50+/-7) degrees. Outside this phase it stays below the 99% minimum detectable polarization. The measured angle agrees with the ionization cone/jet direction (~45 degrees), and spectro-polarimetric modeling favors a soft-band origin for the polarization. The Stokes Q/I and U/I modulation is well described by a cosine at the orbital period and favors two spatially separated polarized components over a single one varying in amplitude. We also tested whether differential Faraday rotation of the disk light in an ordered magnetic field can reproduce the modulation and used it to place upper limits on the magnetic field. These results show that soft-band polarization of LMC X-1 appears only near inferior conjunction at a position angle aligned with the disk normal, and highlight the importance of orbital-phase sampling in polarimetric studies.
